newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Analysts say Astra facing struggle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Analysts say Astra facing struggle.

text.p: Swedish drug company Astra AB posted worse-than-expected results for the first half of 1997 and the company faces an uphill battle to fill the gap that will be left when its key drug, ulcer agent Losec, matures, analysts said on Friday.

A 13 percent rise in sales to 21.47 billion crowns ($2.7 billion) was in line with expectations but a four percent lift in pre-tax profits to 7.01 billion crowns was lower than the consensus market forecast of 7.18 billion.

Analysts were particularly disappointed by an operating profit of 6.75 billion crowns for the six months to June 30 against 6.30 billion crowns a year ago with operating margins in the second quarter under 30 percent versus 32 percent.

"The numbers were a bit disappointing...especially as people were expecting to see a rebound from a weak first quarter that was affected by stockpiling late 1996," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Steve Putnam.
"The Astra story is starting to look more and more suspect," said Putnam who has rated the stock a "sell" for the past few months.
Astra's share tumbled on the report, trading 10.5 crowns lower to 142 crowns by 1230 GMT.
Analyst James McKean at Morgan Stanley said the lightness of the report was understandable with the company increasing spending on new products and pushing products through the pipeline quicker.

In the first half, expenditure on research and development (R&D) rose 22 percent to 3.99 billion crowns as Astra tried to fill the gap that will be left when its top selling drug, Losec, matures and its patent expires in 2001.

"I would be quite relaxed about this report if the growth rate was going to accelerate but I am not convinced that what they are doing will accelerate growth," said McKean who has a neutral recommendation on Astra.
"They are doing all the right things strategically but there is a lot of uncertainty out there.
"I think we will see more of the same in the future. I don't think things are going to change dramatically."
Analyst Jan Dworsky from CI Nordic Securities said he had been negative on Astra for some time and this report confirmed his view.

He said anti-peptic ulcer agent Losec performed well, with world sales rising to 14.72 billion crowns from 11.78 billion and Astra's own sales, excluding its sales in the U.S. with Merck Inc, climbing 17 percent to 10.02 billion crowns.
But Dworsky said respiratory drug sales were disappointing, up seven eight percent to 4.01 billion crowns with anti-asthma Pulmicort rising eight percent to 2.48 billion.
"We are negative on the stock and will continue to be so for sometime," Dworsky said.
"They are increasing R&D expenditure to try to fill the pipeline with new products but they will face an uphill struggle with Losec maturing and its patent expiring.
"They face an enormous challenge given the size of Losec and I think they will continue to struggle and underperform the sector in terms of sales and earnings progressively."
Putnam said it did not look like Astra's R&D had yet produced anything to bale the company out.

"They may have to start to look at corporate measures, with talk about whether they are a possible takeover target for the cash flow or whether they could try to take over the complete Astra/Merck joint venture," Putnam said.
"They are in a bit of a strategic bind."
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1045 ($ = 8.019 Swedish Crowns)
